original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Five sources and all 31 nonzero masks, one common exact F2-linear B, paired A readouts, and paid elementary source XORs restoring all source rows. Construct ten B queries with twelve XORs; prove nine impossible even with arbitrarily many XORs.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one added operation family. Elementary source XORs change the read-only-source restriction. A common B is an explicit narrower hypothesis needed to implement combined source masks; the old heterogeneous B_j contract is not claimed.
bottleneck_link: A legally paid source-mixing operation can replace expensive repeated recursive queries. This is a central connector-interface pilot but has no identified selected-supplier instance and no new moment or kappa.
stop_rule: Bounded nested-shear pilot at 500000 candidates; then one exact difference-basis formulation at dimension five. Stop after an attaining word and complete nine-point exclusion; do not search higher dimensions or claim an optimal XOR count. Reserve final quarter for validation and handoff.
evidence: PROOF.md; CERTIFICATE.json; verify.py; independent.py; test_package.py; VALIDATION.md. Exact free-algebra identity both directions; 2600 normalized nine-point sets checked twice by distinct algorithms; 3024 dense matrix cases; explicit complete-tariff fixture.
author: Arham Tahir
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in algebra, research, both implementations, tests and writing. No subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: Does an actual supplier provide a common B and temporarily owned source rows with favorable complete source-XOR prices?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only such a boundary can turn the abstract query reduction into a supplier improvement.
open_questions.first_step: Trace two original common-B calls, their frames/source-access contracts and one fully charged XOR including routing and precision; check the price inequality in PROOF.md.
open_questions.blocked_by: No selected-supplier instance or physical admission is established; mandatory read-only sources or unfavorable tariffs falsify that candidate.

open_questions.question: What is the least restored source-XOR count among ten-query five-source paired-readout words?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Twelve is only an attained count; a smaller paid bill could improve the interface threshold.
open_questions.first_step: Use exact source-basis plus connector-state synthesis, with a complete finite domain and explicit counterexample controls.
open_questions.blocked_by: No complete synthesis or XOR-count lower bound is supplied; pursue only if actual tariffs justify it.

local_claim.question: Can explicitly restored source XORs escape the read-only five-source connector boundary at favorable full prices?
local_claim.method: Exact source-coefficient paths, complete normalized difference-basis exclusion, free noncommutative replay and dense matrix oracle.
local_claim.domain: F2, five source rows, 31 masks, arbitrary exact common B and A_m, paired readouts; construction has ten B and twelve XORs.
local_claim.expected_artifact: This scoped package and focused PR.
local_claim.posting_limitation: No connected Discussion-write tool; public start-here/list/handoff reads available. No authenticated browser action was attempted.
local_claim.timing: Initial 500000-candidate exploratory pilot preceded structured TASK.json completion; the exact question and added operation had been stated in commentary. Structured claim completed before final proof/certificate validation.

pilot.family: Ten B queries interleaved with four source shears in nested inverse pairs; random words plus randomized two-occurrence words.
pilot.interpretation: Bounded search failure only; not an exclusion of four-XOR words.
pilot.followup: Nine-point coordinate-normalized full census; ten-point cover and a Hamming tour chosen for an explicit attainable twelve-XOR implementation. No search-completeness claim for XOR synthesis.

initial_overlap.limits: PR titles/bodies including drafts; local top-level READMEs/TASK metadata and ledger; not arbitrary diffs, all closed PRs, or complete discussion comments.

predecessor_credit: Ross Richardson PR943/934; PR889 dirty fanout and shhxera/CubeJerry; Chafik Boukhalfa PR628; Douglas Colkitt PR1185 (unchanged six-source alphabet); Hanson Sun PR1215 (independent six-source verification); retained framework and supplier authors.
result_summary: Scoped construction and finite-exclusion proof; ten paired-readout B calls are sharp. Twelve source XORs are attained, not proved optimal. Both earlier repairs and full dirty recursive words pass.
